approach.method_basis: A genetic algorithm run directly on molecular graphs. It keeps a population of molecules that have already been scored by the objective, samples breeding parents from the high-scoring end of that population, and builds new candidates by cutting two parents apart and recombining connected fragments, and by making small local edits to atoms and bonds. Everything generated is sanitised, canonicalised and sent straight to the oracle; whatever comes back with a good score is merged into the population and the weakest members are dropped. There is no surrogate model, no pretrained network, no library of catalogue molecules to rank, and no cross-task memory: the only thing that steers the search is the scores of the molecules this run has itself already paid for.
approach.novelty: The method statement leaves the selection pressure, the population bookkeeping and the failure handling open, and this implementation fixes all three. Parents are drawn from three declared high-ranked score bands rather than from a single elite cut, so breeding stays broad while still being score-directed. Survival is greedy on a bounded population of sixty-four, seeded only from the ten scored molecules supplied at the start, with accepted offspring merged the moment their scores arrive so the very next batch already breeds from them. Proposals that come back invalid or already-seen are replaced by generating more molecules from the same operators, never by falling back to a fixed reserve list. Seven distinct atom and bond mutation operators sit alongside fragment crossover, and every breeding event logs its parent ranks, operator provenance and parent-beating outcome so the selection pressure can be checked after the fact rather than assumed.

observed_bottleneck: There is no parent or campaign evidence yet. The benchmark difficulty is to turn a small set of scored initial molecules and a limited task-local feedback budget into improving de novo structures. The proposed root tests whether repeated graph edits and recombination around highly ranked observed molecules exploit this feedback quickly enough for final Top-1 improvement.
hypothesis: Evolve a task-local population of scored molecular graphs by sampling breeding parents across high-ranked score quantiles, generating de novo offspring with graph crossover and atom/bond mutation, and greedily retaining the highest-scoring observed survivors after each feedback batch.

finding_summary.headline: Plain graph evolution with no learned model ranks third of thirteen Discovery roots, and every intended behaviour activated
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a strong, cheap baseline. Against the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, which span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root sits third at 0.4917, within 0.019 of the best method in the round, and it did that with no pretraining, no corpus-trained generator, no surrogate and no learned policy. That reframes what the more elaborate lineages have to justify: any learned component now has to earn its place against direct selection on task-local scores, not against a naive baseline. The interesting tension is that activation was clean while efficiency was not. Roughly six in seven oracle calls went to molecules that did not beat the parent that made them, and the mean offspring was worse than its parent, so the strong result comes from occasionally getting lucky at scale rather than from reliably climbing. That is precisely the bottleneck a proposal-filtering mechanism would attack, and it is the most concrete Development target this root produces. What is still open: one seed only, so no reliability claim and no anchor decision; no paired comparison against any other algorithm; and the retry machinery was never stressed, since the longest rejection streak was two, so behaviour on an exhausted or hostile neighbourhood is untested.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.4917 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.5989 on deco_hop, 0.9051 on drd2_docking, 0.2083 on median_2, 0.3315 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4145 on zaleplon_mpo. All four pre-registered observables moved in the intended direction and the falsifier was not triggered. Parent selection was strongly score-directed: across 2225 breeding selections the mean topness percentile was 0.883 against a uniform baseline of 0.5, an enrichment of +0.383, and all three declared quantile bands were used on every task. Both operator families produced offspring on every task, with crossover behind 0.439 and atom/bond mutation behind 0.743 of the 1450 emitted molecules; 74 outer retries were needed for 1524 attempts. Feedback demonstrably changed the search: 1025 offspring were admitted to the population immediately, 432 distinct admitted offspring were later chosen as parents 2084 times, and reuse began in batch 2 on every task. Final population best rose above initialization everywhere, most sharply on drd2_docking (0.0190 to 0.9051) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.0021 to 0.3315). The one weak number is local improvement: only 201 of 1450 offspring, or 13.9 percent, strictly beat their best breeding parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent difference was -0.084.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, aromatic, entirely achiral molecules that converge hard onto one inherited scaffold per run, with an unstable-motif tail
molecular.overall_character: Across all five runs the generator emits ring-heavy, strongly aromatic molecules: ring-closure rate 0.92 to 0.99 and aromatic-atom rate 0.89 to 0.96 in every run, with essentially no cumulated double bonds (0.000 to 0.007). Mean SMILES length varies widely by run, from 38.8 to 70.2, which shows the graph operators do grow and shrink molecules in response to feedback. What each run converges on is recognisably a decorated descendant of one of the ten molecules it started with: the top twelve structures in a run typically share a complete skeleton and differ only in single-atom substituent swaps. Two systematic absences stand out. Stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs, so the generator never writes a stereochemical assignment even when it builds tetrahedral ring-fusion carbons. Charged-atom rate is also exactly 0.000 everywhere, so no ionised or zwitterionic forms are ever proposed. Alongside the plausible majority there is a persistent tail of chemistry a bench chemist would reject outright: peroxide and trioxide chains, N-hypofluorite groups, S-O-N linkages, and degenerate one- and two-atom fragments that still consume oracle calls.

per_task.generated_character: Almost every proposal is a 6-5 fused bicyclic heteroaromatic carrying an aryl carboxamide. The entire top of the run is one indole or azaindole 2-carboxamide anilide skeleton rewritten with methyl, ethyl, methoxy, fluoromethyl and halogen swaps, and that skeleton is visibly a decorated version of the best molecule the run was handed at the start.
liabilities: Peroxide O-O linkages introduced by crossover between two aromatic cores
Bare one- and two-atom fragments such as elemental halides submitted as candidates
Thioamide substitution of the amide carbonyl, giving a metabolically unstable analogue
missing_features: No ring systems beyond the inherited bicycle - no bridged, spiro or tricyclic cores are ever built
No stereodefined sp3 centres anywhere in the run
No basic or ionizable side chain to balance the neutral amide core
No ring-size variation, since every new ring closed is five- or six-membered
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks how completely the inherited skeleton survives. The three structures tied at 0.4145 all keep the fused bicycle, the ring NH, the exocyclic amide and the 4-fluoroanilide intact and differ only at one substituent. The zero tail is either a one- or two-atom fragment or an oversized crossover product that fused two whole copies of the scaffold together, so the objective gives no partial credit for half a scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The run settles on the xanthine, or purine-2,6-dione, core carried in from the starting set. It is N-aminated with a halogenated aminopyridine and decorated with a second aryl or heteroaryl ring, and most of the top structures also hang a conjugated polyene or enamine tail off the core. Mean SMILES length reaches 56.6, so molecules here grow substantially larger than their parents.
liabilities: N-hypofluorite groups written on the imide nitrogen, which is not a real functional group
Long conjugated polyene tails built by repeated mutation at the same site
Peroxide and N-N-O chains formed by blind heteroatom substitution
missing_features: No saturated or partially saturated linker to place the decoration out of the core plane
No stereochemistry on the sp3 centres it does create
No ring systems beyond fused five- and six-membered rings and simple biaryl links
No acidic or basic ionizable group anywhere in the run
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The objective barely separates anything: the whole run lies between 0.500 and 0.599, and the starting molecules already scored 0.500 to 0.548, so the entire 29-batch search bought about 0.05. Everything sitting exactly at the 0.500 floor is a one- to three-heavy-atom fragment, which means the score behaves mostly as a has-any-structure indicator with a small decoration bonus on top.

per_task.generated_character: This is the one run whose winners look like a real receptor-ligand series. The strongest structures pair a 2-aryl-pyridine with an N-alkyl pyrrolidine or piperidine basic amine, several carrying a free carboxylic acid on the connecting carbon. Molecules are the largest of the five runs at mean length 70.2, and the ring-closure rate is the highest at 0.986.
liabilities: Aryl thiol substituents on the biaryl tail, which would oxidise readily
S-O-N chains produced by heteroatom substitution on the aromatic ring
Free aldehyde groups retained on high-scoring structures
missing_features: No stereochemistry, despite genuine tetrahedral centres in the winning series
No explicit protonated ammonium form of the basic amines
No conformationally constrained bicyclic amine head groups
No aromatic ring systems larger than a single biaryl pair
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises steeply with the presence of a protonatable N-alkyl saturated amine attached to a biaryl tail. The 0.905 and 0.884 structures both carry exactly that pair, whereas the 0.0004 to 0.002 tail retains the aromatic halves and has lost the basic nitrogen entirely. Adding halogen and thiol decoration to the tail while keeping the amine moves the score only within the 0.72 to 0.91 band, so the amine is the discontinuity and the decoration is fine-tuning.

per_task.generated_character: One fused polycyclic aminal-plus-cyclic-urea cage bearing an ethoxy-substituted aryl arm dominates the entire top of the run. The twelve best differ only in whether individual ring carbonyls are C=O or C=N, whether the aryl arm is propyl or butanoyl, and whether an extra amino group is present. Halogen rate is 0.145, the lowest of the five runs, so the generator essentially stopped using halogens here.
liabilities: Aminal N-CH2-N motifs at the heart of every top structure, which would hydrolyse readily
Cumulated allene-type double bonds appearing in a small fraction of proposals
Enamine C=C linkages conjugated into the ring carbonyls
missing_features: No aromatic variation beyond an unsubstituted or amino-substituted phenyl ring
No halogen substitution anywhere on the winning series
No stereochemistry on the several sp3 ring-fusion atoms in the cage
No alternative cage topology - the same fused system is reused for the whole run
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The band is extremely narrow, 0.2008 to 0.2083 across the whole top twelve, while the losing tail is trivially small - a single carbon, acetonitrile, ethanol, isopropyl chloride. So the gradient rewards keeping the complete cage plus arm assembled and is almost flat once that assembly exists, which is why the search plateaued at 0.2038 for batches 14 through 21.

per_task.generated_character: Compact, heavily oxygenated fused polycyclics: a methoxylated benzene fused to an imidazole and to a dioxole or dioxane ring, usually with one fluorine sitting on a ketal-like carbon. Mean SMILES length is 38.8, the shortest of the five runs, and the aromatic rate drops to 0.886, so this run built more saturated ring content than the others.
liabilities: Peroxide and trioxide chains such as O-O-O-C appearing in the zero-scoring tail
Orthoester and ketal carbons carrying both a fluorine and two alkoxy groups
One- and two-atom fragments submitted as candidates and consuming oracle calls
missing_features: No trifluoromethyl or polyfluorinated aliphatic groups
No primary aliphatic amine or amide nitrogen chain
No stereochemistry, although the chemistry this objective rewards is stereodefined
No open-chain flexible backbone - almost everything proposed is caged
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 0.331 winner and its 0.271, 0.250 and 0.238 followers are the same tetracyclic ketal-imidazole with the fluorine and methoxy positions permuted, so the run is a single-scaffold decoration search. Everything at zero is either a single atom, a diatomic, or an oversized dimer built by crossover, and the median score of 0.031 against a best of 0.331 shows how sharply the objective drops away from that one cage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five independent runs, across 1450 proposed molecules, even though the winning series in several runs contain genuine tetrahedral carbons - a substituted pyrrolidine attached to a biaryl, ring-fusion carbons in a fused aminal cage - where configuration would change the chemistry entirely.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no concept of stereochemistry at all
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set writes only flat connectivity. A generator that can address three-dimensional chemistry needs mutation operators that set, invert and permute tetrahedral and double-bond configuration as first-class edits, and a novelty check that treats two configurations of the same skeleton as distinct molecules rather than as a duplicate to reject.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every run the entire top twelve share a complete ring skeleton that is visibly present in one of the ten molecules the run was handed at the start, and successive improvements only swap single substituents on it. Where a new ring does appear it comes from fusing two copies of an existing core together, which produced oversized dimers that scored zero.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rings are inherited and decorated, never invented
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Fragment recombination plus atom and bond edits can decorate a skeleton but cannot construct an unseen ring system, so the reachable chemistry is bounded by whatever ring systems the starting molecules happen to contain. A generator would need ring-construction and ring-breaking operators, or a fragment source outside the current population, to reach scaffolds not present at initialization.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Bare one- and two-atom species - a chlorine atom, a diatomic interhalogen, a single carbon, acetonitrile, ethanol - were emitted as candidates and consumed oracle evaluations, scoring zero every time. At the other extreme, crossover produced dimers well over 140 characters that also scored zero. Both extremes appear in the worst-scoring set of multiple runs.
transferable_gaps.gap: No control over what counts as a submittable molecule
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Validity is being checked only as chemical sanitisation, which a lone halogen passes. A generator spending a fixed evaluation budget needs a size and complexity floor and ceiling on emitted structures, so that operator accidents are rejected and regenerated locally instead of being paid for at the oracle.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Peroxide and trioxide chains linking two aromatic rings, N-hypofluorite groups written onto an imide nitrogen, and S-O-N chains on an aromatic ring all appear among the proposed molecules, in some cases inside otherwise reasonable structures. These are products of substituting one heteroatom for another without any check on the resulting local environment.
transferable_gaps.gap: Blind heteroatom substitution creates motifs that cannot exist as stable compounds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation alphabet treats all heteroatom swaps as equivalent. A generator would need a substructure-level plausibility screen applied after each edit, rejecting known-unstable local environments before the molecule is proposed, which costs nothing at the oracle and removes a systematic slice of wasted budget.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Within each run the twelve best molecules differ from one another by single-atom substituent swaps, and the population best plateaus for long stretches - fifteen consecutive batches with no improvement in one run, eight in another - while the population mean keeps creeping up. The search is refining a single basin rather than testing alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Selection collapses onto one skeleton and cannot recover breadth
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Greedy score-ranked survival on a bounded population removes structural variety faster than the operators can regenerate it, so the population converges to near-duplicates and breeding produces near-duplicates in turn. A generator needs an explicit diversity term in survival, a similarity cap on the retained population, or a restart mechanism, so that budget spent after a plateau is spent somewhere new.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The charged-atom rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs. Carboxylic acids and basic amines do appear, but always drawn in their neutral forms, and no quaternary, zwitterionic or explicitly ionised species is generated anywhere in 1450 molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: No ionizable or charged chemistry is ever proposed
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operators never place a formal charge, so a whole region of chemistry - permanently charged head groups, zwitterions, salt forms - is unreachable regardless of how the objective scores. A generator intended to cover ordinary medicinal chemistry needs charge-setting edits and a canonicalisation policy that preserves them.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
